notes: Summary: Velaris is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a realtime customer-facing assistant embedded in product. Primary focus: deterministic latency SLOs + reserved GPU economics for peak trading hours.
Business needs: low tail latency during market-open spikes, predictable unit cost for reserved capacity, ability to failover to cheaper model without UX regressions.
Latency SLO discussion (detailed):
- Non-streaming (batch-like requests): customer wants p50 <= 70ms, p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 450ms measured end-to-end (app SDK -> response complete).

- Streaming (progressive token delivery): Velaris cares about time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and per-chunk latencies. Proposed SLOs: TTFB p95 <= 120ms, per-chunk p95 <= 40ms; p99 targets flagged as advisory (investigate with POC).

- Measurement alignment: major debate — Velaris prefers client-side timing (SDK) because it reflects UX; Redwood recommends server-side canonical timestamps with correlation IDs and edge ingress/egress timestamps for unbiased SLA. Agreed: POC will collect both and compare delta (client - server).

- Definition notes: agree to publish SLOs in two flavors: 'observed UX SLO' (client SDK timing) and 'server SLO' (Redwood ingress -> egress). Dispute points: network jitter attribution, CDN/edge latencies, and mobile client variability.
Throughput & reserved GPU planning:

- Target steady throughput: 450 req/sec average during peak; burst envelope up to 1,200 req/sec for 5 minute windows. Typical request size ~350 tokens input, 150 tokens output average (context-heavy).

- Redwood proposal: 8 x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs (mixed vms) with autoscale headroom + 2x burst buffer for 10-minute spikes. Customer asked for explicit per-GPU token/sec profiles and per-route concurrency limits.
- Acceptance criteria for POC: sustain 500 req/sec for 6 hours with p95 non-streaming <= 220ms and no more than 0.2% p99 violations attributable to platform (not network).
SLA negotiation items:
- Credits: Velaris requests SLA credits tied to user-impacting SLOs (p95 and p99 tiers) and a clarified incident classification matrix for latency-related outages.
- Rollout window: they want ramped deployment with canaries and auto-fallback to hosted model variant during incidents. Redwood to define fallback model parity and expected quality delta.
POC plan & telemetry:
- 2-week POC on dedicated pool in us-east-1; Redwood to supply testing harness and synthetic load scripts (open-source).

- Telemetry: collect server ingress/egress timestamps, per-request KV cache hit/miss flag, GPU utilization, per-shard queue length, and SDK-side timings. Velaris will also run production-like mobile web agents to capture client timing.
- Artefacts: hold a joint measurement appendix with CSV exports and raw traces. Include Fireflies transcript id ff_2026-02-20_3254 for initial scoping call.
Risk notes & technical concerns:
- Warm start p99 spikes from KV cache cold-warm transitions — suggested mitigation: pre-warm cache during scheduled market opens and buffer for first 5k requests.
- Streaming p99 measurement ambiguity — need to define per-chunk vs end-to-end p99 and how partial failures are counted.
- Multi-tenant noise: request isolation and cgroup limits; Velaris wants hard isolation on reserved pool or explicit noisy-neighbor mitigation.
Customer quotes (paraphrased):
- 'We can't tolerate >300ms p95 for our in-product assistant during trading hours — perception matters.'
- 'Deterministic billing on reserved GPUs is a must — finance needs predictable monthly burn.'
Action items assigned:
- Diego (SE): produce detailed per-GPU throughput matrix + recommended pool sizing (due 2026-03-07).
- Sara (AE): push procurement timeline and get procurement checklist from Velaris (due 2026-03-10).
- Legal/Compliance: prepare data residency addendum (us-east-1) and provide example SOC2 artifacts (Lina to coordinate).
- Joint eng sync scheduled: 2026-03-08 10:00 ET — agenda: measurement definitions, POC test plan, rollout gating.
